subject.mainFocus: Problem-Solving Therapy for Suicide Prevention curriculum, exercises, measures, and visual models
subject.description: A concept-based study guide reconstructed from a hard-copy VA PST-SP Veteran packet. It organizes the curriculum into toolkits, exercises, measures, visuals, and reusable workflows.

documentSummary.purpose: Preserve and reorganize the PST-SP Veteran packet as a readable, searchable, and extensible study guide without requiring a page-for-page reproduction.
documentSummary.scope: Core curriculum, optional handouts, major exercises, selected visuals, source coverage, and measures through the substantially complete photographed packet.
documentSummary.summary: The guide presents PST-SP as a staged workflow: recognize stress and risk, stabilize emotional activation, restore hope and cognitive capacity, define the real problem, generate and evaluate options, act, review, and prepare for future stress. It also catalogs exercises, measures, visual models, and source coverage.
intendedAudience: clinicians or educators reviewing the program structure
readers interested in structured problem solving
documentSummary.confidence: high for core curriculum; moderate-to-high for the final measures tail

keyPoints.title: PST-SP is a staged workflow
keyPoints.description: The curriculum stabilizes emotion and cognition before asking the participant to solve complex problems.

keyPoints.title: Each obstacle maps to a toolkit
keyPoints.description: Negative emotion, hopelessness, brain overload, and ineffective problem solving are matched to specific toolkits.

keyPoints.title: The guide is concept-based
keyPoints.description: Multiple source pages are synthesized into coherent chapters and exercises rather than reproduced page by page.

keyPoints.title: Measures remain clinically contextual
keyPoints.description: The measures are summarized as assessment instruments and are not presented as stand-alone self-diagnostic tools.

concepts.name: Stress as load exceeding capacity
concepts.definition: Stress emerges from the relationship between demands and available coping capacity.

concepts.name: State-dependent problem solving
concepts.definition: Problem-solving ability depends on emotional and cognitive operating condition.

concepts.name: Externalization
concepts.definition: Move information out of working memory into persistent external forms so the mind can process rather than store.

concepts.name: Realistic optimism
concepts.definition: A constructive problem orientation that recognizes difficulty while preserving the possibility of useful action.

concepts.name: Iterative problem solving
concepts.definition: Action outcomes are reviewed as information; unsuccessful attempts lead to revision rather than global failure conclusions.

general.summary: A practical guide to how PST-SP helps a person move from emotional overload and hopelessness toward deliberate action and review.
keyPoints: Calm and organize before trying to solve.
Identify the obstacle and use the matching toolkit.
Prepare for future stress rather than waiting for crisis.

technical.summary: A structured knowledge model of a staged human problem-solving workflow with state regulation, cognitive load reduction, decision support, action, feedback, and contingency planning.

clinicalContext.summary: This guide reorganizes and summarizes PST-SP participant materials. It is not an official VA publication and does not replace treatment, clinical judgment, safety planning, or emergency care.
clinicalContext.intendedUse: Personal study, curriculum review, and documentation of the PST-SP program structure.
limitations: The source packet was reconstructed from photographs of a hard copy.
A small tail of the Measures section was not photographed.
Some content is summarized rather than reproduced.
Personal handwritten responses are not treated as canonical program content.
safetyNotes: Use clinical measures only in their intended context.
Use a Safety Plan and immediate support when risk has escalated into crisis.
Do not treat this guide as a substitute for professional care.

toolkits.title: Stop and Slow Down
toolkits.purpose: Interrupt emotional escalation and restore enough control for deliberate thinking.
whenNotToUse: as a substitute for Safety Planning during an active crisis

toolkits.title: Visualization for Hope and Motivation
toolkits.purpose: Make a positive and possible future state emotionally available.

toolkits.title: Overcoming Brain Overload
toolkits.purpose: Reduce cognitive load so the person can reason, organize, and decide.
whenToUse: when too much must be held in mind

toolkits.title: Planful Problem Solving
whenToUse: after sufficient emotional and cognitive stabilization
whenNotToUse: during an active crisis before safety needs are addressed

toolkits.title: Review and Future Forecasting
toolkits.purpose: Consolidate skills, check beliefs, anticipate stressors, and plan continued use.

exercises.title: Safe-Place Visualization
exercises.purpose: Reduce arousal and create a mentally safe environment before problem solving.

exercises.title: Deep Diaphragmatic Breathing
exercises.purpose: Reduce physiological arousal through slow abdominal breathing.
preparation: optional hand placement on chest and abdomen

exercises.title: Intentional or Fake Yawning
exercises.purpose: Use repeated intentional yawning as a brief calming and focusing technique.
steps: continue until natural yawning or reduced tension

exercises.title: Mindful Meditation
exercises.purpose: Observe thoughts and emotions without treating them as facts or commands.
practiceGuidance: the goal is not an empty mind

exercises.title: Progressive Muscle Relaxation
exercises.purpose: Recognize and release physical tension through alternating contraction and relaxation.
practiceGuidance: practice daily for at least one week
safetyNotes: do not tense to the point of pain or cramping

exercises.title: Mindful Wabi-Sabi Walk
exercises.purpose: Use walking and sensory awareness to cultivate present-moment attention and acceptance of imperfection.

exercises.title: Visualization for Hope and Motivation
exercises.purpose: Imagine a positive and possible future that is slightly better than the present.
practiceGuidance: return to the image when hope decreases

exercises.title: Externalize
exercises.purpose: Move information out of working memory into visible, persistent forms.
steps: write, list, draw, photograph, record, or discuss the information

exercises.title: Simplify
exercises.purpose: Break a large problem into smaller, manageable problems or steps.

exercises.title: Visualize to Clarify a Problem
exercises.purpose: Explore a vague problem from multiple dimensions before solving it.
steps: ask what, where, when, why, how, and who

exercises.title: Visualize to Practice in Your Mind
exercises.purpose: Mentally rehearse a skill, procedure, or conversation before real-world execution.

exercises.title: Problem-Solving Worksheet
exercises.purpose: Define a problem, generate options, choose a plan, act, and review the outcome.
whenToUse: when a practical problem can be addressed
practiceGuidance: use another worksheet if the first plan is not satisfactory

exercises.title: Future Forecasting
exercises.purpose: Anticipate changes and match likely challenges to PST-SP tools before escalation occurs.

exercises.title: Motivational Worksheet
exercises.purpose: Externalize ambivalence by comparing the benefits and costs of moving forward and not moving forward.
whenToUse: when a useful action has been identified but motivation remains low
